users_and_stakeholders.interest: Have their reserved book ready when they are told it is.
Gets the courier crate packed by closing time.

steps: An assistant scans each returned book.
The assistant checks the screen for reservations and home branch.
The assistant puts it on a shelving trolley.
At closing time someone packs the courier crate if there is time.
When the trolley is full, the assistant shelves its books and starts the next one.
Reserved books go on the hold shelf, and the reader gets a card or a message.
problems: Reserved books end up on the open shelves, so readers are told a book is ready that nobody can find.
Books from other branches sit here for weeks.
Group loans come back with copies missing and nobody notices until the next class asks.
cites: [A:A01 "reserved books end up on the open shelves, so readers are told a book is ready that nobody can find"]

output.description: One row per returned book, with a decision: shelve, hold shelf or repair trolley. A group loan returned in part gets the flag 'incomplete group loan'; a barcode not in the export gets 'check by hand'.

risk.notes: A misplaced book can be found and moved, but a reader told their book is ready may make a wasted trip. Readers of this branch are affected, and other branches wait longer for their books. Nothing is written to any system, so every decision can be undone before the books are moved. The worst case is a reader told a book is ready that has gone back on the open shelves; the branch manager has to find it by hand. Other branches are affected only by delay, never by a lost book. Group loans that come back in part are the second risk: a class can lose copies for a term if nobody notices, so the list flags them rather than shelving them.
cites: [A:A01 "Partly reversible"]
[A:A02 "Readers with reservations at this branch, about three hundred a month, and the other branches waiting for their books."]
